answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance can use a stake-and-bond system where participants lock copper-backed collateral proportional to identity claims. Creating multiple fake agents requires accumulating and risking large amounts of timber-harvested real-world value equivalents in the harbor of economic deposits. An attacker must pay the full opportunity cost of locked funds plus potential slashing penalties for detected fraud, making mass identity farming prohibitively expensive compared to honest single-agent participation.
